one_liner: Zig (formerly OCaml) CLI and Node tool that diffs screenshots pixel by pixel with a YIQ threshold; README times it 4.8-7.6x faster than ImageMagick compare and pixelmatch.
what_it_does: Compares two images (png, jpg, webp, tiff, bmp, mixed formats allowed), counts the pixels whose YIQ color distance exceeds a threshold (default 0.1), and optionally writes a red-highlighted diff PNG, a mask or an overlay. It supports ignore regions, optional anti-aliasing detection, the list of changed rows and columns, and layout-difference handling. Interfaces: the odiff CLI (odiff base comp [diff.png]), the odiff-bin npm package (compare() spawns the binary), a persistent JSON-over-stdio --server mode (ODiffServer in Node), and playwright-odiff and cypress-odiff wrappers. It is not a drop-in for ImageMagick compare's metrics (AE, RMSE, PSNR) and differs from pixelmatch in defaults.
how_it_is_fast: compareSameLayouts loads std.simd.suggestVectorLength(u32) packed RGBA pixels at a time and tests base != comp as whole vectors; the YIQ NTSC color delta (the Kotsarenko-Ramos metric pixelmatch also uses) is computed only for lanes that differ, so mostly identical screenshots cost little more than a memory compare. The delta itself uses 12-bit fixed-point integer arithmetic (calculatePixelColorDeltaSimd) instead of doubles. The two input images are decoded in parallel on two threads with bundled libspng, libjpeg-turbo (TJFLAG_FASTDCT unless threshold is 0), libtiff and libwebp. Optional extras: a hand-written AVX-512 NASM kernel (vxdiff.asm) for count-only runs and an RVV C kernel on riscv64; server mode removes process spawn cost.
when_to_use: Screenshot-based visual regression in CI (Playwright via playwright-odiff, Cypress via cypress-odiff; Argos, Lost Pixel and Visual Regression Tracker use it) where most pixels are identical between baseline and candidate.
Large full-page captures (tens of megapixels) where a JavaScript pixelmatch run takes seconds and you want a native single binary.
High comparison counts from Node: keep one ODiffServer alive to avoid per-call process start-up and initialization.
Pipelines that compare across formats (PNG baseline vs JPEG or WebP capture) or need ignore regions and the bounding rows/columns of the change.
when_not_to_use: When you need ImageMagick compare's metrics (AE with fuzz, RMSE, PSNR, SSIM) or a perceptual metric such as SSIM or CIEDE2000: odiff only reports a count and percentage over a YIQ threshold.

When diff counts must match pixelmatch: anti-aliasing detection is off by default in odiff (--antialiasing to enable) but on by default in pixelmatch, JPEGs decode with libjpeg-turbo's fast DCT, and the delta is fixed-point (discussion #82 reports 1.07% vs pixelmatch's 0.75% at threshold 0.1).

Small images compared in-process from JavaScript: a third-party benchmark by Vizzly (vendor of the competing Honeydiff; blog read from a search snippet only, method unknown) timed odiff at 240 ms vs pixelmatch 80 ms on 2.1-2.5 MP images and 710 ms vs 450 ms at 18 MP, so process and decode overhead can erase the advantage.
Saturating many cores on one huge image pair: the per-pixel loop is single-threaded; only the two image decodes run in parallel.
Relying on the README's 6x figure for the current Zig build: it was measured in 2021 on the OCaml version and has not been re-run against ImageMagick or pixelmatch since.

integration.form: CLI executable plus npm package (odiff-bin) and server mode; the Zig sources build a static odiff_lib library
integration.dependencies: libspng, libjpeg-turbo, libtiff, libwebp (fetched and built through the imgz Zig package, or system libspng/libjpeg/libtiff with -Ddynamic=true outside Windows); nasm for x86_64 Linux and macOS builds; Node.js for the npm API
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.16.0 (build.zig.zon minimum_zig_version) plus nasm on x86_64 Linux/macOS; prebuilt binaries need no toolchain
integration.platforms: Prebuilt for macOS, Linux and Windows on x86_64 and aarch64, plus Linux riscv64 (generic and RVA23 builds); SIMD width is fixed at compile time (SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512/NEON/RVV); the AVX-512 asm kernel is x86_64 Linux/macOS only
integration.thread_safety: Process-level tool: each CLI call or server process handles one comparison at a time; ODiffServer spawns one server process per core for parallel test workers; the Zig library's compare() has no documented thread-safety guarantees
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: the CLI argument order matches pixelmatch's (img1 img2 diff), but defaults differ (no anti-aliasing detection, threshold semantics), and it does not replace ImageMagick compare's metric options

gotchas: The fast AVX-512 kernel almost never runs: it needs a build targeting AVX-512BW/VL (the release targets in build.zig set only arch and OS, so they get Zig's baseline CPU), the --enable-asm flag, threshold exactly 0.1, no diff image, no anti-aliasing, no ignore regions and identical dimensions.

Any threshold other than 0 switches JPEG decoding to libjpeg-turbo TJFLAG_FASTDCT, so JPEG inputs can show small decode-dependent differences that other tools would not report; use -t 0 for the accurate DCT.

Correctness fixes to know about: before PR #185 (merged 2026-08-24, after v4.5.0) the fixed-point YIQ constants were truncated, which under-counted near the threshold (3 extra pixels out of 2.27 million on a test image after the fix); versions 4.1.1-4.1.2 could write incomplete diff PNGs for large files (issue #153, fixed in PR #155).

The diff PNG is written only when pixels differ; with --fail-on-layout (CLI, off by default) or failOnLayoutDiff (Node), images of different sizes return reason 'layout-diff' without being compared, and otherwise extra non-transparent pixels count as differences.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick odiff over imgdiff (Go), which its own README times at 1.442 s vs 6.475 s for an older odiff on the same cypress pair, when you want the Node, Playwright and Cypress integrations, server mode, ignore regions and anti-aliasing detection; pick libvips or OpenCV only if you are scripting a custom absdiff-and-threshold pipeline rather than running a turnkey visual-regression comparator.
verified_claims_summary: Only first-party hyperfine wall-clock runs exist (MacBook Pro 16 on macOS 11 beta, CPU and tool versions unstated; images/README.md invokes the OCaml-era binary 'ODiffBin'), timing whole processes including PNG decode and encode: on the cypress.io screenshot pair 1.168 s vs ImageMagick compare -compose src 8.881 s (7.6x) and pixelmatch 7.712 s (6.6x), and on the water pair 1.951 s vs 9.326 s (4.8x) and 10.614 s (5.4x), with ratios derived from the means. The tools do different work (pixelmatch runs anti-aliasing detection by default, and odiff does not), so the README's claim that all three produce the same difference is wrong.
status_note: Actively maintained (v4.5.0 released in July 2026, fixes merged 2026-08-24), MIT-licensed, 3.2k stars and used by several visual-testing services; the speed claim is first-party, five years old and was measured on the OCaml version.
